limits: The boolean changes planned settings; it is not a timer, destroy command or proof services stopped. The operator must verify actual zero running tasks and absent one-off bootstrap tasks before destructive actions.
Apply a separately reviewed non-destructive transition first, then prepare and review a distinct actual-state destroy plan. No destroy plan or real Terraform apply was run by this task.
Normal deployment source bytes changed, so regenerate the initial saved application plan rather than applying an older source-bound artifact.

Skipping the final snapshot and deleting current automated backups does not remove existing manual/recovery snapshots, old retained backups, restore-test instances or copied data; inventory and review those separately.

The six Terraform-managed runtime secret recovery settings do not control the RDS-managed master secret. AWS states RDS deletes that secret and associated metadata when the database instance is deleted; verify actual deletion afterward.

Forced secret deletion is irreversible and asynchronous; changing this setting alone does not delete a secret or establish eventual removal. Scheduled-deletion secrets have no charges while marked for deletion; do not invent a seven-day recovery storage charge.

S3 force_destroy removes operations objects and versions irreversibly on eventual destroy; it must be successfully applied into resource state beforehand. Retained Terraform state remains independent and sensitive.
Encryption, private networking, logging/retention and task execution behavior are otherwise unchanged. No new services or telemetry enablement is included.
